summary: Confirmed the writer/predicate mismatch but corrected its shape: the sole active .orchestrator-handoff.json writer (H9 hard-mode wrap-up) emits a flat top-level continuation_path string per context/contracts/wrap-up.md, while orchestrate-triage-classify.sh and skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md Stage 4 check only nested continuation_context.handoff_path -- a key that writer never emits. validate-handoff.sh already accepts both forms. Recommends Option B: extend the classifier and base SKILL.md's mirrored predicate to accept continuation_path OR continuation_context.handoff_path, rewrite handoff-schema.md to document both, and separately flag cslib's Stage 5 template which never populates any continuation pointer at all.
decisions_made: Recommend Option B (relax classifier predicate to accept continuation_path OR continuation_context.handoff_path), not Option A (force all writers onto nested form) -- validate-handoff.sh already precedents dual acceptance
handoff-schema.md needs a full rewrite of its continuation_context section, not a patch, since it documents only the form the sole active writer never emits

Dispatch-context normalization (skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md line 410 passing continuation_context to the next implement dispatch) is separate implementation work beyond the predicate fix and must be its own plan phase

cslib-implementation-hard-agent.md's Stage 5 template never populates any continuation pointer on partial/blocked (hardcoded null, no instruction) -- flag as a related but separable defect, do not silently fold into this task
The task's phrasing 'continuation_context.note' is not a literal field anywhere in the tree -- it describes the substance of the markdown handoff at continuation_path/handoff_path, not a JSON key
